title: An empty brand cut mask names the existing opaque proof recovery instead of recommending detail-destroying solid recolouring
steps: Run the existing cut and recolour tool tests, including the synthetic ring-and-bar zero-mask recovery and fitting regression.
expect: A transparent-source cut with an empty fill mask refuses inversion and names the actual readable opaque proof and exact cut_mark arguments.
Recutting that proof with the existing tool produces a nonempty mask; default inversion preserves distinct ring, internal bar and enclosed-fill tones before a real markOnly fit.
The fitted output has the kit's 2x geometry and every original source, mask and proof remains unchanged.
A missing, transparent or unreadable proof does not produce a fabricated recovery path, and the refusal warns that solid mode discards internal detail and still requires image review.
Default and explicit solid modes remain available for lettermarks; no passing reviewer record or acceptance verdict is fabricated.
fence: Use existing tools and proofs only; preserve the approved prompt, existing thresholds, original images and independent image review. Mechanism PASS is not site or visual acceptance.

tests: recolour_mark: an empty mask points to the existing opaque proof, whose recut supports a detailed inverse and fit
recolour_mark: an empty mask without an opaque proof warns about detail loss without offering a fabricated recovery
recolour_mark: palette mode for an icon recolours only the colours that do not read; solid for a lettermark
